### Insights and directions

**Starting point.** (1) Preserve embedding/scoring hooks and expose the actual trained module. Comparable diagnostics require architecture-compatible features. (2) Training margins cannot establish sustained-interest relevance. Controlled prefix perturbations test model dependence, not causal preferences. (3) Feedback suggests broad associations and unsupported compatibility assumptions. Histories establish interactions; text provides incomplete specifications, not ownership or purchase necessity.

**Related work.** (1) Recency analysis [1] motivates testing accumulated evidence without assuming optimal recency weights. (2) Sampled-metric research [2] requires separating diagnostic margins from pinned HR@10 and full-catalog usefulness. (3) ECCR [3] separates complementarity from compatibility. HGN/HAM [4,5] establish precedent for gated or pooled historical preferences, weakening novelty claims.

Three directions remain: accumulated-interest modeling, controlled dependence diagnostics, and evidence-aware inspection.

### Framework

| Layer | Existing approach | Proposed addition | Remaining uncertainty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Representation | SASRec sequence encoding | Recurrence-weighted residual | Lexical recurrence is a proxy |
| Diagnosis | Margins, cosine alignment | Matched history perturbations | Dependence is not preference |
| Evidence | Broad associations | Literal specification checks | Missing facts remain unknown |
| Selection | Pinned macro HR@10 | Paired comparisons | Sampling and selection uncertainty |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality / future potential / implementation difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder.

1. **Recurring-interest residual: 4/6/6.** Originality: targeted combination, but substantial pooling/gating precedent [4,5]. Potential: interpretable intervention, but lexical shortcuts and new-interest suppression remain possible. Difficulty: small branch, but causal computation, calibration and export parity require care.
2. **Matched perturbation probes: 4/7/4.** Originality: task-specific controls, but established sensitivity analysis. Potential: actionable evidence, but no accuracy guarantee. Difficulty: reusable hooks, but position/count matching is consequential [1].
3. **Specification evidence flags: 5/6/6.** Originality: useful abstention adaptation, but established compatibility reasoning [3]. Potential: clearer explanations, but sparse evidence limits coverage. Difficulty: transparent rules, but heterogeneous specifications complicate precision.

### Selected proposal: recurring-interest residual

At 0% progress, retain this modest, falsifiable intervention; novelty and gains remain unestablished. Fit fixed, normalized TF–IDF on training-item titles/descriptions. Recurrence weights pool **ID embeddings**; text supplies weights and remains available at inference.

```text
S = masked TFIDF cosine matrix; remove actual diagonal
for causal prefix ending at t:
    recurrence[j] = sum(S[j,k], k <= t) / max(valid_count-1, 1)
    weights = normalize(exp(-decay*age) * (epsilon+recurrence))
    pooled = weighted_sum(ID_embeddings, weights)
    features = SASRec_features + tanh(alpha)*norm_matched(pooled)
optimize original next-item loss; initialize alpha = 0
```

Use five arms: baseline, full residual, recency-only, uniform pooling, and fixed within-category shuffled text. Uniform pooling averages ID embeddings; it is not a new text-embedding branch. Match residual capacity/settings and allocate the 43,200 GPU-second budget before runs. Require gains over controls before attributing benefits to recurrence. Report category/macro HR@10; when host hit records are available, use 10,000 paired within-category bootstrap resamples. Intervals exclude training and adaptive-selection uncertainty [6]. Prespecify history-length, text-availability and training-popularity strata without subgroup tuning.

Fix preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, routing, splits, candidates and epoch default 200. Preserve DATA_DIR, trial-local artifacts, predictor parity and DiagnosisProbe. Validate causal prefixes, padding, repeats, missing text and truncation; restore diagnostic model mode and mark missing observations unavailable. No improvement is claimed.

idea.description: Add a bounded, zero-initialized recurring-interest pooling residual to each causal SASRec representation. Fixed training-corpus TF–IDF similarities and recency determine weights over historical ID embeddings; retain the branch at inference and test its contribution against matched pooling and shuffled-text controls.
idea.motivation: Feedback suggests that broad associations and isolated interactions sometimes displace sustained interests. This intervention tests whether explicit accumulated evidence improves the mandated validation objective without assuming unavailable traits, ratings, equipment ownership or purchase necessity. HGN and HAM establish substantial component-level precedent, so the contribution would be empirical evidence about causal lexical recurrence rather than a claim of a fundamentally new model class.
idea.implementation_notes:
Keep os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], original input splits, all four dataset routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and SASREC_EPOCHS environment default 200. Write every artifact beneath the trial directory and use a single GPU. No test labels, external datasets or downloaded pretrained weights are used. Fit one fixed TF–IDF transform per category on unique items occurring in training histories, using only titles and descriptions. Freeze and serialize vocabulary, IDF, preprocessing parameters and item-vector mapping; transform other publicly available item text with this frozen transform. Document the exact tokenizer, token pattern, n-gram range, minimum document frequency and feature cap before execution. Missing text produces a zero vector, whose similarity is defined as zero. The branch uses TF–IDF only for history weights and pools the existing trainable item embeddings; it remains active at inference.

For each retained length-L sequence, compute a masked L-by-L nonnegative cosine matrix from L2-normalized fixed text vectors. Explicitly zero padding rows/columns and subtract the actual diagonal, retaining similarities between distinct occurrences of a repeated item. For every valid position t, accumulate similarities only over valid positions through t, divide by max(prefix_count-1, 1), and combine recurrence with exponential recency weights using a strictly positive epsilon. Normalize over valid positions; empty prefixes return zero. With fixed text features, incremental prefix sums require O(L²) arithmetic after similarity computation, rather than repeatedly recomputing prefix matrices. Avoid dense catalog-wide similarities; sparse gathered prefix vectors are sufficient. Any neighbor truncation changes the algorithm and must be documented and held fixed. Use exactly the baseline's retained events, padding, learned-position indexing and final valid-position scoring. Sliding windows must remove departing interactions from recurrence sums. Define recency by retained-event position initially, rather than introducing timestamp parsing as an additional experimental factor.

Replace the near-saturated sigmoid gate with tanh(alpha), initialized at alpha=0. At each position, match the pooled vector's RMS norm to the detached base-feature RMS using epsilon-protected normalization; explicitly mask invalid positions. Document that gradients pass through the pooled-vector normalization but not the base norm. At initialization, the gate receives gradients, while additional branch gradients begin after the gate moves from zero; shared item embeddings continue receiving baseline-loss gradients. Retain the baseline dimension, loss, optimizer and other settings initially. A nonsaturated sigmoid with a small external scale is a possible later ablation, not an additional unbudgeted default experiment.

Prespecify five arms: unchanged SASRec; full recurrence residual; recency-only residual with recurrence disabled; uniform ID-embedding pooling with both recency and recurrence disabled; and the full residual with a seed-fixed within-category item-to-text permutation. The original phrase 'uniform text pooling' is corrected because this architecture does not pool text embeddings. All residual arms share trainable capacity, normalization, initialization, optimizer and training allowance; the unchanged baseline necessarily lacks the added scalar. Disable the residual in evaluation mode as a functional baseline-equivalence check. Allocate the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget across arms before execution, accounting for failures, diagnostics, checkpoint evaluation and any tuning. Estimate feasibility from accounted runtime; if five comparable arms cannot fit, report incomplete mechanistic evidence rather than imply that all controls ran. Fix checkpoint cadence, selection rule and tuning allowance beforehand, counting every comparison. Select solely through the host's pinned macro validation HR@10 with 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42. Do not change the host evaluator. Report per-category scores and their unweighted mean; call them sampled-candidate results.

If the host exposes per-user validation hits, preserve paired records and use 10,000 bootstrap resamples of users within each category, recomputing macro differences. Report 95% intervals, absolute percentage-point differences and discordant wins/losses. These intervals condition on checkpoints, training seed and candidates; they exclude training variability and adaptive-selection bias. If hit records are unavailable, omit intervals rather than reconstruct or invent them. Prespecify strata by training-history length, history/target text availability and target training frequency; report counts without subgroup tuning. Baseline improvement alone does not establish semantic recurrence as the mechanism. Gains over recency-only, uniform and shuffled-text controls provide stronger evidence, with uncertainty still reported. Boilerplate, duplicate titles and popularity correlations remain possible shortcuts despite IDF weighting. Generic-token removal, duplicate-title filtering and popularity-only comparisons are optional follow-ups only if explicitly budgeted.

Serialize model parameters, residual configuration, text-transform artifacts and dataset routing beneath the trial directory. Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py executes the identical retained-prefix feature path. Verify optimized recurrence against brute-force prefixes and compare exported predictor scores with the training-side model using identical checkpoints, category routes, metadata transforms, padding, masks and evaluation mode. Cover repeated IDs, all-padding sequences, empty metadata, one-event prefixes and truncated windows. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. view.model must be the actual nn.Module; view.item_emb, log2feats and predict_score must expose the trained architecture. Restore the model's previous training mode after diagnosis and mark absent observations unavailable rather than successful zeros. Category breakdowns remain unavailable because item categories are not provided. Treat mean cosine and logit margins as descriptive, scale-dependent probes, not validated quality measures.

For auxiliary dependence probes, use chronological training-only prediction prefixes and fixed candidate sets. Exclude previously observed items using the original prefix's exclusion set even after perturbation, while retaining the held-out training-prefix target. Compare recurrence-based, isolated-item and recent-window masks against repeated count-matched random masks, matching positions where feasible. Compare position-preserving masking with deletion/repacking and report rank changes alongside overlap. Full-catalog training-prefix probes are auxiliary and must fit the budget. Twenty simulator users, five per category, receive full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for descriptive inspection; they do not establish population preferences. Literal compatibility or redundancy flags require supporting title/description spans, distinguish explicit incompatibility from unknown evidence, and cannot establish ownership, replacement intent or whether a need is satisfied.
idea.pseudocode:
Prespecify arms, TFIDF settings, epsilon, decay, norm epsilon, checkpoint rule and GPU budget
For each category:
    fit frozen TFIDF on titles/descriptions of unique training-history items
    serialize transform and item mapping under trial directory
    initialize baseline SASRec and alpha = 0
    for sequence, positive, negative in training batches:
        base = sasrec.log2feats(sequence)
        valid = sequence != 0
        X = frozen_text_vectors(sequence)
        S = cosine(X, X), with zero-vector cosine defined as zero
        zero S rows/columns for padding
        subtract actual diagonal of S
        for supervised position t:
            prefix_mask = valid AND position <= t
            recurrence[j] = sum(S[j,k] for valid k <= t) / max(prefix_valid_count-1, 1)
            raw[j] = exp(-decay * retained_position_age(j,t)) * (epsilon + recurrence[j])
            weight = normalize raw over prefix_mask; empty prefix yields zero
            pooled[t] = sum(weight[j] * item_embedding(sequence[j]))
        residual = pooled / clamp(RMS(pooled), norm_epsilon)
        residual *= detach(RMS(base))
        features = valid_mask * (base + tanh(alpha) * residual)
        optimize original baseline next-item loss using features
    export predictor with identical feature path and routing
Run prespecified matched controls within the shared budget
Select checkpoints using only pinned host macro validation HR@10
If paired validation hits are exposed, bootstrap users within category 10000 times
Report category scores, macro differences, uncertainty limitations and completed controls

originality.positive: The causal lexical recurrence weighting and controlled diagnostic design form a targeted, falsifiable adaptation to the reported sustained-interest failure.
originality.negative: Gating, recency weighting, historical pooling and item–item relationships have substantial precedent in HGN, HAM and related methods; exact-combination novelty remains unestablished.

future_potential.positive: A successful controlled result could motivate adaptive interest timescales and provide interpretable evidence about when lexical recurrence contributes beyond ID-history pooling.
future_potential.negative: Sparse or generic text, repeated-item shortcuts and exploration behavior may limit transfer; the method does not directly solve compatibility, complementarity or purchase-necessity reasoning.

code_difficulty.positive: The architecture adds only a scalar gate and deterministic weighting around the existing encoder, embeddings and objective.
code_difficulty.negative: Efficient causal prefix computation, numerical calibration, exact truncation semantics, diagnostic adaptation, matched controls and predictor parity make the complete experiment substantially harder than the small architectural change suggests.

related_work.title: [1] Oh and Cho (2024): recency-bias analysis in sequential recommendation
contributions: Introduces a recency-bias metric and reports that excessive emphasis on recent items can harm recommendation accuracy.
Motivates comparing recency-only pooling with recurrence-aware accumulated evidence and controlled history perturbations.
limitations: Does not establish optimal recency weighting for these four Amazon datasets.
History sensitivity measures model dependence, not causal user preferences.

related_work.title: [2] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled evaluation can produce model comparisons inconsistent with full-catalog evaluation.
Motivates preserving the mandated selection metric while treating sampled margins and full-catalog diagnostics separately.
limitations: Does not prescribe an architecture improvement for this task.
Does not justify changing the host's pinned candidate sampling or evaluator.

related_work.title: [3] ECCR: Explainable and Coherent Complement Recommendation Based on Large Language Models
contributions: Distinguishes broad complementarity from specific relevance and compatibility.
Motivates evidence-aware inspection of unsupported compatibility assumptions.
limitations: Its language-model approach is not adopted because this task prohibits fetching pretrained weights.
Available histories and sparse descriptions cannot establish current ownership or purchase necessity.
Lexical recurrence alone does not implement its compatibility reasoning.

related_work.title: [4] Hierarchical Gating Networks for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Combines long- and short-term preferences, feature and instance gates, and item–item products.
Establishes component-level precedent that lowers the originality assessment for gated historical pooling.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed causal TF–IDF weighting and SASRec residual combination.
Its results do not demonstrate gains on this pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: [5] HAM: Hybrid Associations Models for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Combines general preferences with pooled recent associations.
Motivates simple ID-history pooling controls before attributing gains to textual recurrence.
limitations: Reported accuracy and runtime advantages are specific to its experiments.
Does not establish whether text recurrence improves the target SASRec baseline.

related_work.title: [6] On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how optimizing finite-sample model-selection criteria can introduce selection bias.
Supports fixed comparison budgets and labeling adaptively selected validation improvements exploratory.
limitations: Does not quantify selection bias for these particular checkpoints or datasets.
Paired user bootstrap intervals do not remove the adaptive-selection problem it describes.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents bootstrap confidence-interval computation and paired resampling.
Supports resampling paired user outcomes within each category before recomputing macro differences.
limitations: Correct implementation still requires preserving category strata and model pairing.
User resampling conditions on trained models and candidate sets; it does not capture training variability or adaptive selection.

related_work.title: scikit-learn TfidfVectorizer documentation
contributions: Documents vocabulary fitting, IDF weighting and L2 normalization.
Provides the fixed sparse representation used for dot-product cosine similarities.
limitations: Lexical overlap is not semantic equivalence, compatibility or purchase intent.
IDF weighting does not guarantee removal of boilerplate or popularity proxies.

related_work.title: ReZero is All You Need: Fast Convergence at Large Depth
contributions: Introduces zero-initialized scalar residual gating.
Motivates replacing a nearly saturated sigmoid with a gate having nonzero derivative at initialization.
limitations: Does not establish recommendation gains for this architecture.
The proposed bounded tanh gate is an adaptation, and residual normalization still requires explicit specification.

related_work.title: Original SASRec implementation
contributions: Provides reference behavior for sequence masking, learned positions and sequence-feature scoring.
Highlights why retained-history indexing and training/inference parity require verification.
limitations: The actual RecHarness baseline remains authoritative for this task.
Reference implementation behavior cannot substitute for checking the exported predictor against its trained checkpoint.
